title: Consensus Hong Kong 2026: Dates, Speakers, What to Expect
description: Consensus Hong Kong 2026 runs February 10 to 12 at the HKCEC. Here are the dates, venue, announced speakers, summits and how to attend, in one place.
body:
Hong Kong — Consensus Hong Kong 2026, the Asia edition of CoinDesk's flagship crypto conference, runs February 10 to 12, 2026 at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre in Wan Chai. It is the event's second year in the city, and the organizer is planning for 15,000 attendees after reporting nearly 10,000 at the 2025 debut. The week puts the exchanges, asset managers, regulators and builders active in Asia in one district.

## At a glance

- Dates: February 10 to 12, 2026 (stages and exhibition floor on February 11 and 12)
- Venue: Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, 1 Expo Drive, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
- Organizer: CoinDesk
- Expected scale: 15,000 attendees from more than 100 countries and more than 100 speakers (organizer-reported)
- Format: six stages, four summits, the EasyA Consensus Hackathon, CoinDesk PitchFest and an exhibition floor
- Official site: [Consensus Hong Kong 2026](https://consensus-hongkong2026.coindesk.com/)

## How the three days of Consensus Hong Kong 2026 run

The conference floor is open for two of the three days. Tuesday, February 10 is the institutional day: the invitation-based [Hong Kong Institutional Summit hosted by Consensus x SALT](https://consensus-hongkong2026.coindesk.com/institutional-summit/) takes place at the Grand Hyatt, early pass pick-up runs at the convention center from 1:00 pm to 8:00 pm, and the official opening party starts at 7:00 pm in Central.

The stages and the exhibition floor run on Wednesday, February 11 and Thursday, February 12. The [official agenda](https://consensus-hongkong2026.coindesk.com/agenda/) places four summits on two stages: the Future of Finance Summit and the AI and Robotics Summit on February 11, then the Global Bitcoin Summit and the Asia Macro Summit on February 12. Deep dives on tokenization, stablecoins, privacy and trading fill a third stage. Dates and coverage are on the [Consensus Hong Kong 2026 conference page](/conferences/consensus-hong-kong-2026).

## Who is on the Consensus Hong Kong 2026 program

CoinDesk's first full lineup release, issued on January 26, counted more than 100 speakers. They include Lily Liu, president of the Solana Foundation; Richard Teng, co-CEO of Binance; Justin Sun, founder of TRON; Peter Mintzberg, CEO of Grayscale Investments; and Ella Zhang, head of YZi Labs. Earlier announcements added Tom Lee of Fundstrat, Bullish CEO Tom Farley and Animoca Brands co-founder Yat Siu.

The agenda also lists a keynote from the Financial Secretary of the Hong Kong SAR, Paul Chan Mo-po, and a fireside with Julia Leung, CEO of the Securities and Futures Commission. The [organizer's speaker list](https://consensus-hongkong2026.coindesk.com/speakers) is still growing, and our [guide to the speakers](/press/consensus-hong-kong-2026-featured-speakers) picks twelve to plan around.

## What is new for the second edition

The clearest change is size. The organizer says the 2026 edition takes the convention center's largest floor, and it reported that the 2025 debut generated an estimated HK$275 million for the local economy.

Several programs sit around the main stages:

- Solana Accelerate APAC, a full-day conference on February 11 at the same venue, with more than 45 sessions listed on [the Solana event page](https://solana.com/accelerate/hong-kong)
- The EasyA Consensus Hackathon, with demos and awards on February 12
- CoinDesk PitchFest, a startup competition with its finals on the main stage
- The Consensus Cup, an evening at Happy Valley Racecourse on February 11 for badge holders
- Guided tours of Shenzhen's tech ecosystem, listed in the organizer's release

## The themes: institutions, stablecoins and machines

The January release names five themes: institutional adoption, DeFi, stablecoins, robotics, and the point where AI agents meet onchain execution. Announced sessions include Tokenizing the Planet, on real-world assets, and Ethereum Next Steps, on scaling and user experience. In practice, February 11 leans toward finance, policy and AI, and February 12 toward Bitcoin, Asian markets and founders.

## How to attend: tickets, registration and side events

Registration is through the official site. Passes are sold in tiers: Pro, Platinum and Piranha, plus a Startup Package. Prices rise in stages as the event approaches, so check the current figure before budgeting.

The organizer projects more than 350 side events across the city during the week. Most run on Luma with host approval, and the official evenings require a Consensus badge. Our [guide to the side events](/press/consensus-hong-kong-2026-side-events) shortlists the ones worth the travel time.

## Frequently asked questions

### When is Consensus Hong Kong 2026?

Consensus Hong Kong 2026 runs from Tuesday, February 10 to Thursday, February 12, 2026. February 10 holds the Institutional Summit, pass pick-up and the opening party. The stages and exhibition floor run on February 11 and 12.

### Where is Consensus Hong Kong held?

The conference is at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, 1 Expo Drive, Wan Chai, on Hong Kong Island. The Institutional Summit on February 10 is at the Grand Hyatt Hong Kong, and the official parties are in Central and Wan Chai.

### Who is speaking at Consensus Hong Kong 2026?

Announced speakers include Lily Liu of the Solana Foundation, Richard Teng of Binance, Justin Sun of TRON, Peter Mintzberg of Grayscale Investments, Tom Lee of Fundstrat and Hong Kong's Financial Secretary, Paul Chan Mo-po. The organizer counts more than 100 speakers across six stages.

title: Consensus Hong Kong 2026 Speakers: 12 Names to Watch
description: Twelve Consensus Hong Kong 2026 speakers to plan around on February 11 and 12, with confirmed roles, session titles, stages and times in Hong Kong.
body:
Hong Kong — Consensus Hong Kong 2026 opens on February 10 at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, with its stages running on February 11 and 12 and more than 100 speakers announced by organizer CoinDesk. These twelve are the ones to plan around, each with the confirmed role and the session slot the organizer has published so far.

## At a glance

- Dates: February 10 to 12, 2026 (stage sessions on February 11 and 12)
- Venue: Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
- Organizer: CoinDesk
- Expected scale: 15,000 attendees and more than 100 speakers (organizer-reported)
- Official site: [Consensus Hong Kong 2026](https://consensus-hongkong2026.coindesk.com/)
- Speaker list: [all speakers announced by the organizer](https://consensus-hongkong2026.coindesk.com/speakers)

Times are Hong Kong time, from the [official agenda](https://consensus-hongkong2026.coindesk.com/agenda/), and can move. Event details are on our [Consensus Hong Kong 2026 conference page](/conferences/consensus-hong-kong-2026).

## Hong Kong's regulators at Consensus Hong Kong 2026

### Paul Chan Mo-po, Financial Secretary, Hong Kong SAR Government

Paul Chan Mo-po is the Financial Secretary of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the official responsible for the city's budget and financial policy. The agenda lists his keynote on the Auros Mainstage on Wednesday, February 11 at 11:55 am. It is the government's statement of priorities for the sector.

### Julia Leung, CEO, Securities and Futures Commission

Julia Leung leads the Securities and Futures Commission, the regulator that licenses virtual asset trading platforms in Hong Kong. She was previously Under Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury. Her fireside follows the Financial Secretary on the Auros Mainstage on February 11 at 12:10 pm.

## Wall Street and treasury names on the main stage

### Tom Lee, Co-Founder and Head of Research, Fundstrat

Tom Lee co-founded Fundstrat in 2014 and runs its research. He is also chief investment officer of Fundstrat Capital and chairman of Bitmine Immersion Technologies. His keynote is on the Auros Mainstage on February 11 at 1:10 pm, and the agenda says he will set out a bull case for bitcoin.

### Peter Mintzberg, CEO, Grayscale Investments

Peter Mintzberg has led Grayscale Investments since 2024, after serving as global head of strategy for Goldman Sachs Asset and Wealth Management. He also sits on Grayscale's board. His session, The Intersection of TradFi and Crypto, is on the Auros Mainstage on February 11 at 11:35 am.

### Tom Farley, CEO, Bullish

Tom Farley runs Bullish, the listed digital asset exchange group that owns CoinDesk, and was president of the NYSE Group from 2014 to 2018. He appears with SkyBridge Capital founder Anthony Scaramucci in The Institutions Are Here on the Auros Mainstage on February 11 at 10:10 am.

### Joseph Chalom, CEO, SharpLink

Joseph Chalom joined SharpLink in July 2025 after two decades at BlackRock, where he worked on its bitcoin and ether funds. SharpLink holds ether as a treasury asset. He speaks with Consensys CEO and Ethereum co-founder Joseph Lubin in Ethereum and the Treasury Revolution on the Auros Mainstage on Thursday, February 12 at 11:25 am.

## Network leaders: Solana, Ethereum, Sui and TRON

### Lily Liu, President, Solana Foundation

Lily Liu is president of the Solana Foundation and a co-founder of Anagram. She is on the Auros Mainstage on February 11 at 9:45 am with Solana's 2026 Outlook and Internet Capital Markets Vision, then joins the panel Building the Solana Supercycle in Asia on the Spotlight Stage at 2:00 pm.

### Hsiao-Wei Wang, Co-Executive Director, Ethereum Foundation

Hsiao-Wei Wang joined the Ethereum Foundation in 2017 as a researcher and worked on the Beacon Chain and the move to proof of stake. She is now co-executive director. Her session, Ethereum Next Steps: Scaling and UX, is on the Auros Mainstage on February 12 at 11:05 am.

### Evan Cheng, CEO and Co-Founder, Mysten Labs

Evan Cheng co-founded Mysten Labs, the original contributor to the Sui network, after leading engineering teams at Apple and research at Meta's Novi unit. He is on the Auros Mainstage on February 11 at 1:30 pm in Beyond the DAT: Driving Ecosystem Velocity with NASDAQ, ETFs, and DeFi.

### Justin Sun, Founder, TRON

Justin Sun founded TRON, one of the networks most used for stablecoin transfers, and advises the exchange HTX. His session, Building Resilient Blockchain Infrastructure for a World in Constant Change, is on the Auros Mainstage on February 12 at 1:55 pm. Payments teams that settle in stablecoins have the clearest reason to attend.

## Exchanges and Asian capital round out the Consensus Hong Kong 2026 speakers

### Richard Teng, Co-CEO, Binance

Richard Teng is co-CEO of Binance. Before joining the exchange in 2021 he ran the financial regulator at Abu Dhabi Global Market and held senior roles at the Singapore Exchange and the Monetary Authority of Singapore. His fireside with Consensus chairman Michael Lau is on the Auros Mainstage on February 12 at 4:00 pm.

### Yat Siu, Co-Founder and Executive Chairman, Animoca Brands

Yat Siu co-founded Animoca Brands, the Hong Kong-based gaming and Web3 investment group, and is its executive chairman. His session, The Case for a Multi-Asset DAT, is on the Auros Mainstage on February 11 at 1:45 pm. The agenda says Animoca is betting that investors in treasury companies want exposure beyond bitcoin and ether.

## How to plan your two days

Wednesday, February 11 carries the policy and institutional sessions. Thursday, February 12 is the day for Ethereum, TRON and Binance. For the rooms outside the venue, see our [guide to the side events](/press/consensus-hong-kong-2026-side-events) and for passes and logistics the [pre-event briefing](/press/consensus-hong-kong-2026-pre-event).

## Frequently asked questions

### Who is speaking at Consensus Hong Kong 2026?

The organizer has announced more than 100 speakers. They include Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po, SFC CEO Julia Leung, Lily Liu of the Solana Foundation, Richard Teng of Binance, Justin Sun of TRON, Tom Lee of Fundstrat and Peter Mintzberg of Grayscale Investments.

### When do the main stage sessions take place?

Stage sessions run on Wednesday, February 11 and Thursday, February 12, 2026, from the morning to about 5:00 pm Hong Kong time. Tuesday, February 10 is reserved for the Institutional Summit, pass pick-up and the opening party.

### Where can I find the full Consensus Hong Kong 2026 agenda?

The organizer publishes the agenda and the speaker list on the official Consensus Hong Kong site. Sessions can be filtered by date and stage, and the listing changes as speakers are added, so check it again the night before.

title: ETHDenver 2026: Dates, Venue, Speakers and What to Expect
description: ETHDenver 2026 runs February 18 to 21 at the National Western Center in Denver. Here are the dates, tracks, confirmed speakers and how to get a free ticket.
body:
Denver — ETHDenver 2026 opens at the National Western Center in Denver on Sunday, February 15 with three days of BUIDLWeek and Camp BUIDL, followed by the main event from Wednesday, February 18 to Saturday, February 21. It is the first edition at a new venue and the first organized around themed summits, with US financial regulators listed next to Ethereum's core teams. That changes how founders, investors and marketers should plan the week.

## At a glance

- Dates: BUIDLWeek and Camp BUIDL February 15 to 17, 2026; main event February 18 to 21, 2026
- Venue: National Western Center, 4850 National Western Drive, Denver, Colorado
- Organizer: ETHDenver
- Theme: New #BUIDL City
- Tracks: Etherspace, Devtopia, New France Village, Futurllama, Prosperia
- Tickets: free general admission, claimed through the organizer's site
- After the event: SporkDAO Community Mountain Retreat, February 22 to 27
- Official site: [ethdenver.com](https://ethdenver.com/)

## What is new at ETHDenver 2026

The biggest change is the address. ETHDenver has moved from the National Western Complex to the newer National Western Center campus, which the organizer describes as a brand new venue built to support building, learning and connecting in one place.

The second change is the format. The organizer says it is trying an experiment with content this year: each day and each stage is divided into theme-based summits, so attendees can follow one subject for a full or half day. Dates, links and planning notes are on our [ETHDenver 2026 conference page](/conferences/ethdenver-2026).

## Five tracks under the New #BUIDL City theme

The program is organized into five tracks, each with its own stage:

- Etherspace: the user-owned internet
- Devtopia: infrastructure
- New France Village: the future of finance
- Futurllama: future tech and trends
- Prosperia: cypherpunks, solarpunks and communities

On opening day, Wednesday, February 18, the organizer's schedule lists a full-day Decentralized AI summit on the Futurllama Stage and a full-day Stablecoins summit on the New France Village Stage, both starting at 10:00 am. The Prosperia Stage carries a half-day Go To Market summit in the morning and a Summit for Founders from 1:45 pm. For a marketer or a founder raising a round, that makes Wednesday the day to be on campus early.

## Who is on the ETHDenver 2026 program

Policy has a visible place on the [ETHDenver speakers page](https://ethdenver.com/speakers/). Hester Peirce, a commissioner at the US Securities and Exchange Commission, is listed, as are Patrick Witt, executive director of the President's Council of Advisors for Digital Assets at the White House, and Tung Chan, Colorado's securities commissioner.

Ethereum's own institutions are represented by Joe Lubin, co-founder of Ethereum and founder and CEO of Consensys, Tomasz Stańczak, co-executive director of the Ethereum Foundation, Danny Ryan, cofounder and president of Etherealize, and Austin Griffith, founder of BuidlGuidl.

From finance, the list includes Johann Kerbrat, who runs crypto at Robinhood, Caitlin Long, founder and CEO of Custodia Bank, Gordon Liao, chief economist and head of research at Circle, and Maria Shen, general partner at Electric Capital. Zooko Wilcox of Shielded Labs and Charles Guillemet, CTO of Ledger, cover privacy and security. The organizer is still adding names.

## BUIDLWeek and Camp BUIDL come first

The three days before the main event are for builders. Camp BUIDL, which the organizer calls its Web3 training ground, runs February 15 to 17 from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm in the nearby CSU Spur Hydro building, taking students from blockchain basics to a deployable application in time for the BUIDLathon, the hackathon at the center of the week. The schedule also lists SEAL darkMode, a security program, on the Confluence Stage at CSU Spur Hydro on February 16 and 17.

## How to attend ETHDenver 2026

General admission is free. Tickets and applications for attendees, builders, speakers, mentors and judges opened on November 18 and are claimed through [ethdenver.com](https://ethdenver.com/). Side events are collected on the organizer's Official Side Event Calendar on Luma, and most need their own registration.

Two companion guides follow this preview: the [ETHDenver 2026 speakers to watch](/press/ethdenver-2026-featured-speakers) and the [ETHDenver 2026 side events](/press/ethdenver-2026-side-events) worth a place in your week.

## Frequently asked questions

### When is ETHDenver 2026?

BUIDLWeek and Camp BUIDL run from Sunday, February 15 to Tuesday, February 17, 2026. The main event runs from Wednesday, February 18 to Saturday, February 21.

### Where is ETHDenver 2026 held?

At the National Western Center, 4850 National Western Drive, Denver, Colorado 80216. This is a new venue for the event. Camp BUIDL and some BUIDLWeek sessions take place in the nearby CSU Spur Hydro building.

### How much are ETHDenver 2026 tickets?

General admission is free. The organizer's site offers a free ticket to attendees who register, with separate applications for builders, speakers, mentors and judges. This is as listed on ethdenver.com at the time of writing.

### Who is speaking at ETHDenver 2026?

The organizer's speaker page lists SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce, Patrick Witt of the White House, Joe Lubin of Consensys, Tomasz Stańczak of the Ethereum Foundation, Danny Ryan of Etherealize and Johann Kerbrat of Robinhood, among others.

title: Consensus Hong Kong 2026 Side Events Worth Your Week
description: Nine Consensus Hong Kong 2026 side events for February 9 to 13, each with its host, venue, time, how to get in and a link to the registration page.
body:
Hong Kong — Consensus Hong Kong 2026 runs February 10 to 12 at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, and organizer CoinDesk projects more than 350 side events across the city that week. These nine have a clear host, a confirmed venue and a reason to go. They are listed in date order, with access rules and a registration link for each.

## At a glance

- Main event dates: February 10 to 12, 2026, Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, Wan Chai
- Side-event week: Monday, February 9 to Friday, February 13 for the events below
- How access works: most events register on Luma with host approval; official Consensus evenings require a conference badge; institutional forums are by application or invitation
- Official listing: [Consensus Hong Kong 2026 agenda](https://consensus-hongkong2026.coindesk.com/agenda/), which carries the official parties and partner events

Event facts for the conference itself are on our [Consensus Hong Kong 2026 conference page](/conferences/consensus-hong-kong-2026).

## Monday, February 9: the day before Consensus Hong Kong

### Liquidity 2026

Hosted by LTP through its Hong Kong subsidiary LiquidityTech, this institutional summit on digital, tokenized and traditional markets runs from 8:00 am to 5:30 pm at the JW Marriott Hotel Hong Kong in Admiralty. It suits trading firms, hedge funds, custodians and exchanges. Entry is ticketed, with complimentary buy-side passes subject to approval. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/ykvpk50b)

### The Realized Summit

Hosted by 499, Pharos Network and RedStone, this one-day conference covers real-world assets, PayFi and the overlap of AI and Web3. It takes place at Soho House Hong Kong, 33 Des Voeux Road West, Sheung Wan. Listed speakers include Pharos Network CEO Wish Wu and RedStone co-founder Marcin Kazmierczak. Registration is through Luma. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/RealizedSummitHK)

## Tuesday, February 10: allocators by day, opening night after dark

### Hong Kong Institutional Summit hosted by Consensus x SALT

CoinDesk and SALT run this closed-door summit at the Grand Hyatt Hong Kong from 8:00 am. The format is keynotes, expert-led roundtables and scheduled one-on-one meetings between investors and asset managers, under the Chatham House Rule. It is built for allocators and fund managers, and participation requires an application and formal approval. [Register or see details](https://consensus-hongkong2026.coindesk.com/institutional-summit/)

### Consensus 2026 Official Opening Night Party

Presented by NOLCHA with CoinDesk at The Trilogy, 26th floor, H Code, 45 Pottinger Street, Central. A networking reception runs from 7:00 pm to 9:00 pm, followed by an after party with live performances and DJ sets. A Consensus badge gives priority access during the reception, and Piranha and Platinum badge holders get express entry. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/ConsensusHK2026Opening)

## Wednesday, February 11: Consensus Hong Kong side events at the venue and the racecourse

### Solana Accelerate APAC

Solana's full-day conference starts at 9:00 am inside the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre. The program lists more than 45 keynotes, panels and lightning talks on payments, institutional finance, DeFi, tokenization and AI infrastructure. It suits builders and fintech teams working on Solana. Ticket details are on the event page. [Register or see details](https://solana.com/accelerate/hong-kong)

### The Consensus Cup at Happy Valley Racecourse

Consensus is an official cup race sponsor at the Wednesday night meeting at Happy Valley Racecourse, and the agenda lists the evening from 6:00 pm to 10:30 pm. Badge holders enter through Gate G to a reserved Beer Garden area with racing and live music. A Consensus badge is required. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/tnq15dxx)

## Thursday and Friday: closing night and the tokenization forums

### The Best Event x Consensus Hong Kong Official Afterparty

The official closing party is on Thursday, February 12 at Pier 1929 in Wan Chai, close to the convention center. Networking for VIP ticket holders, Consensus badge holders and speakers starts at 7:00 pm, with general admission from 9:00 pm. The organizer's agenda says a Consensus badge is required; the Luma page also lists separate tickets. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/TBE-ConsHK26)

### RWA Summit Hong Kong

Hosted by UVECON.VC with LynxCap Investments, this summit on tokenized real-world assets and stablecoins runs February 12 and 13 from 10:30 am to 5:00 pm at Runnovation, Causeway Centre Block B, 28 Harbour Road, Wan Chai. Listed speakers include Joseph Chan, Under Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury, and Yat Siu of Animoca Brands. Standard tickets require approval. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/rwasummithk)

### DAT Summit Hong Kong

Luna PR and Noemi host this invitation-only forum on Friday, February 13 at the Four Seasons Hotel Hong Kong, 8 Finance Street, Central. Registration opens at 8:30 am and programming runs from 9:00 am to 3:00 pm. It is for capital allocators and listed companies working on digital asset treasuries. Some third-party calendars show another date and hotel; rely on the host's page. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/7cuyh87u)

## How to choose your Consensus Hong Kong 2026 side events

Start from one goal. For raising or allocating capital, the Institutional Summit, Liquidity 2026 and the DAT Summit screen who attends. For builders, Solana Accelerate APAC and The Realized Summit are where product teams gather. Independent events run their own registration and need no Consensus pass, so apply early. For what happens inside the venue, see the [pre-event briefing](/press/consensus-hong-kong-2026-pre-event) and our [guide to the speakers](/press/consensus-hong-kong-2026-featured-speakers).

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I get into Consensus Hong Kong side events?

Register on each host's own page, usually on Luma, and wait for approval. Official Consensus evenings such as the Opening Night Party and the Consensus Cup require a conference badge. Institutional forums, including the Consensus x SALT summit and the DAT Summit, are by application or invitation only.

### Are there official Consensus Hong Kong 2026 parties?

Yes. The organizer lists the Opening Night Party at The Trilogy in Central on February 10, the Consensus Cup at Happy Valley Racecourse on February 11 and the official afterparty at Pier 1929 in Wan Chai on February 12.

### When does Consensus Hong Kong side-event week start?

The larger side summits begin on Monday, February 9, the day before the conference opens, and the last forums on this list finish on Friday, February 13. The conference itself runs February 10 to 12, 2026.

body:
Denver — ETHDenver 2026 runs from February 15 to 21 at the National Western Center in Denver, and the week around it fills with summits, builder nights and happy hours. Most are free but need registration or host approval, and the best ones fill early. These ten have a confirmed host, day and time on their own event pages, and are listed in the order they happen.

## At a glance

- Main event dates: February 18 to 21, 2026, after BUIDLWeek on February 15 to 17
- Side-event week: Monday, February 16 to Friday, February 20 for the events below
- How access works: free registration on Luma for most; several need host approval; the ETHVC Summit inside the venue also needs an ETHDenver ticket
- Official listing: [ETHDenver 2026 Official Side Event Calendar](https://luma.com/ethdenver)

## ETHDenver 2026 side events during BUIDLWeek

### The Scaling Summit: House of AI

Hosted by 499 with 0G and Hetu as co-hosts and MetaMask as special partner, this summit runs on Monday, February 16 from 12:30 pm to 6:00 pm at 3330 Brighton Boulevard. The agenda covers AI-native infrastructure and compute, with speakers from MetaMask, Kite AI, 1inch, Gensyn and the Monad Foundation. Registration is free. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/ScalingEthDenver)

### Builder Nights Denver

Francesco Andreoli and Consensys host this evening on Tuesday, February 17 from 6:00 pm to 11:00 pm, presented by MetaMask, Linea and other partners. The provisional agenda lists three panels and a fireside chat with Tomasz Stańczak of the Ethereum Foundation at 7:30 pm. Entry is free, every ticket type needs approval, and the address is shared after registration. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/bndenver)

## Wednesday, February 18: summits on campus, drinks after

### Decentralized AI Summit

Listed on the organizer's official calendar, this summit takes place on the Futurllama Stage inside the main venue on Wednesday, February 18 from 10:00 am to 5:00 pm. It examines how decentralized infrastructure, models and incentives are changing artificial intelligence. Registration on Luma is free. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/n73goivl)

### Stablecoins Summit

Hosted by Refraction IRL on the official calendar, the Stablecoins Summit also runs on Wednesday, February 18 from 10:00 am to 5:00 pm at the National Western Center. It covers the infrastructure, use cases and regulatory questions behind onchain money. Registration on Luma is free. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/vzaat2wi)

### Happy Hour at The Walnut Room with Tectonic and Hack VC

Tectonic, Hack VC and Halborn, with Sushi, Polymarket and Zero Gravity, host drinks at The Walnut Room, 3131 Walnut Street, on Wednesday, February 18 from 4:00 pm to 6:00 pm. It is a short, early slot for security teams and founders who want investor time before dinner. Free, with host approval. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/2akpqrf3)

### Dim Spirit Listening Party at The Blockspace Church

WebZero Events hosts this listening party on Wednesday, February 18 from 7:00 pm to 11:00 pm at The Blockspace Church, which the host describes as a multi-day crypto experience by Polkadot in a renovated church. Dim Spirit plays more than an hour of unreleased tracks, with an open bar and a private chef. Free, with host approval. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/listeningparty)

## Thursday, February 19: quantum security and institutional rooms

### Quantum Summit at ETHDenver

Presented by Tectonic Labs with Hack VC, Halborn, Sushi, Polymarket, Zero Gravity and W3JOE, the Quantum Summit runs on Thursday, February 19 from 10:00 am to 3:30 pm, with five panels between 10:30 am and 2:00 pm. Topics include post-quantum cryptography and privacy technologies, and panelists include Charles Guillemet of Ledger and Jay Jog of Sei. Registration is free and the address is shared with registered guests. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/ez0wln8b)

### ETH Denver VIP Institutional Soirée

Halborn, Blockaid and The Graph host an evening for institutional decision-makers on Thursday, February 19 from 4:00 pm to 7:00 pm, at a venue the hosts place about seven minutes by car from the main conference. The [SEC's public calendar](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/meetings-events/ethdenver) lists Atkins and Commissioner Hester Peirce at ETHDenver on Wednesday, February 18 from 4:00 pm to 4:30 pm Eastern, which is 2:00 pm in Denver.

Peirce has served as an SEC commissioner since January 2018. Earlier in her career she was counsel to Atkins during his own term as a commissioner, and senior counsel on the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs. She is listed alongside Atkins in the SEC's February 18 notice.

### Patrick Witt, Executive Director, President's Council of Advisors for Digital Assets, The White House

Witt leads the council that develops and coordinates national policy on digital assets, according to his organizer biography. His session is the one to attend for teams whose plans depend on federal policy timelines, including stablecoin issuers, exchanges and anyone raising from US institutions.

Chan heads the Colorado Division of Securities and has chaired the fintech committee for state securities regulators. She also served as the first general counsel of the Ethereum Foundation. Founders incorporated in, or raising money in, the host state should make time for her.

title: TOKEN2049 Dubai 2026 Postponed to April 2027: What Changes
description: TOKEN2049 Dubai, planned for April 29-30, 2026, is postponed to April 21-22, 2027. What the organizer said, and what ticket holders and sponsors do next.
body:
Dubai — TOKEN2049 has postponed its Dubai conference, which was due to open on April 29 and 30, 2026 at Madinat Jumeirah, to April 21 and 22, 2027. The organizer announced the move on March 13, less than seven weeks before doors, citing uncertainty in the region and its effect on safety, international travel and logistics. For the companies that had booked tickets, booths, flights and side events around the last week of April, the Dubai plan now shifts by a full year.

## At a glance

- Original dates: April 29-30, 2026
- New dates: April 21-22, 2027
- Venue: Madinat Jumeirah, Dubai
- Organizer: TOKEN2049
- What happens to tickets: Registered tickets carry forward to the 2027 edition automatically; holders can instead request a transfer to TOKEN2049 Singapore on October 7-8, 2026
- Official announcement: [TOKEN2049 Dubai 2026 event update](https://www.token2049.com/dubai/announcement)

## What TOKEN2049 announced on March 13

The organizer's statement says the decision was made with its partners and stakeholders, "in light of the ongoing uncertainty in the region and its impact on safety, international travel and logistics." It adds that preparations were progressing strongly, and that postponing was preferable to running a smaller event than the one attendees expect.

The statement is explicit that the event is postponed, not cancelled. It also restates the organizer's confidence in Dubai as a hub for digital assets and thanks the city's regulators and government partners.

Press coverage placed the decision in the context of the regional security situation. [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/post/393543/token2049-dubai-moved-to-2027-amid-heightened-security-risks-in-uae) Iranian missile and drone strikes affecting Dubai International Airport and the financial district, along with widespread airspace closures. The organizer's own announcement does not describe those events.

## What the TOKEN2049 Dubai postponement means for ticket holders and sponsors

Ticket holders do not need to do anything. Every registered ticket stays valid for the edition now listed on our [TOKEN2049 Dubai 2027 page](/conferences/token2049-dubai-2027). Anyone who would rather attend this year can ask to move the ticket to Singapore through the organizer's [ticket transfer form](https://forms.token2049.com/dxb26/transfer-to-sg26), using the ticket email and ticket number.

The announcement does not set out a refund policy. Questions about tickets, sponsorships and transfers go to info@token2049.com.

For sponsors and exhibitors, the organizer says commitments will be carried forward and that its team is contacting partners directly to coordinate next steps.

## What else moved on the Dubai calendar

TOKEN2049 was not the first to pull back. A day earlier, The Open Network cancelled Gateway Dubai, which had been planned for May 1 and 2, and said it would look at an alternative format later in the year, [according to crypto.news](https://crypto.news/token2049-dubai-pushed-to-2027-over-security-concerns/).

Within the TOKEN2049 series, the change leaves one event in 2026. [TOKEN2049 Singapore](/conferences/token2049-singapore-2026) is confirmed for October 7 and 8 at Marina Bay Sands, and the organizer describes it as the next gathering of its global community.

## What to do now

- Ticket holders: decide between April 2027 in Dubai and October 2026 in Singapore. Staying with Dubai needs no action; moving to Singapore needs the transfer form.
- Sponsors and exhibitors: wait for the organizer's outreach, or contact its sponsorship team with questions.
- Travelers: the organizer recommends contacting airlines and hotels directly to change bookings made for late April.

The page for the [postponed 2026 edition](/conferences/token2049-dubai-2026) stays on our [conference calendar](/conferences) for reference.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is TOKEN2049 Dubai 2026 cancelled?

No. The organizer says the event is postponed, not cancelled. The edition planned for April 29 and 30, 2026 will not take place on those dates, and the next TOKEN2049 Dubai is scheduled for April 21 and 22, 2027.

### When is TOKEN2049 Dubai now?

TOKEN2049 Dubai is now scheduled for April 21 and 22, 2027, at Madinat Jumeirah. The [official TOKEN2049 Dubai site](https://www.token2049.com/dubai) carries updates from the organizer, including the announcement published on March 13, 2026.

### Do TOKEN2049 Dubai tickets carry over?

Yes. All registered tickets carry forward to the April 2027 edition and no action is required. Holders who prefer to attend in 2026 can request a transfer to TOKEN2049 Singapore using the organizer's form. The announcement does not mention refunds.

### Is TOKEN2049 Singapore still happening?

Yes. The organizer confirmed in the same announcement that TOKEN2049 Singapore will take place on October 7 and 8, 2026 at Marina Bay Sands. It is now the only TOKEN2049 conference scheduled for 2026.

title: Bitcoin 2026 in Las Vegas: Dates, Speakers, What to Expect
description: Bitcoin 2026 runs April 27 to 29 at The Venetian in Las Vegas. Here are the dates, confirmed speakers, what is new this year and how the passes work.
body:
Las Vegas — Bitcoin 2026, the annual Bitcoin Conference produced by BTC Inc, opens April 27 and runs through April 29 at The Venetian Convention and Expo Center in Las Vegas. The sitting chairs of the SEC and the CFTC are both on the program, the policy forum returns on the opening day, and the organizer expects its largest crowd to date, which makes this the week when Bitcoin companies, miners, investors and policymakers are all in one building.

## At a glance

- Dates: April 27 to 29, 2026 (Pro Day on Monday, April 27)
- Venue: The Venetian Convention and Expo Center, Las Vegas
- Organizer: BTC Inc, the company behind Bitcoin Magazine
- Expected scale: more than 40,000 attendees and 500+ speakers (organizer-reported projection)
- Format: six stages and six content tracks, from Bitcoin 101 to Enterprise
- Official site: [Bitcoin 2026](https://b.tc/conference/2026)
- Our event page: [Bitcoin 2026 Las Vegas](/conferences/bitcoin-2026-las-vegas)

## Who is speaking at Bitcoin 2026

BTC Inc opened its speaker rollout in February with three names: Michael Saylor, founder and executive chairman of Strategy; Paul Atkins, chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission; and Mike Selig, chairman of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The organizer describes Atkins as the first serving SEC chair to speak at a Bitcoin Conference, according to its [first speaker announcement](https://btcmedia.prowly.com/444479-bitcoin-2026-conference-announces-first-wave-of-world-class-speakers-redesigned-programming-and-expanded-cultural-experience).

As of mid-April the conference site also shows Senator Cynthia Lummis, Strike and Twenty One chief executive Jack Mallers, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino, Blockstream co-founder and CEO Adam Back, Morgan Stanley head of digital asset strategy Amy Oldenburg, American Bitcoin co-founder and chief strategy officer Eric Trump, and David Bailey, CEO and chairman of Nakamoto Inc. Our [guide to the Bitcoin 2026 speakers](/press/bitcoin-2026-las-vegas-featured-speakers) covers who is worth planning around.

## What is new at Bitcoin 2026

Sessions are spread across six stages: Nakamoto, Genesis, Energy, Open Source, Enterprise and Deep, the last reserved for Whale Pass holders. Three additions stand out.

- Compute Village: new to the Bitcoin Conference, a hub for miners, developers and infrastructure companies working on power-dense compute and energy.
- Code & Country on day one: the policy forum returns for a second year on April 27 and is open to Pro Pass and Whale Pass holders only, per the [Code & Country announcement](https://btcmedia.prowly.com/446342-bitcoin-conference-announces-code-country-2026-policy-forum-returns-for-election-year).
- A larger art program: BMAG, the arts and culture division of BTC Inc, is building a 6,000-square-foot gallery whose centerpiece is an original copy of The Times of London from January 3, 2009, the front page referenced in Bitcoin's genesis block.

## The themes: policy, treasuries and compute

The program has six tracks: Bitcoin 101, AI + Compute + Mining, Code & Country, Culture, Open Source and Enterprise.

Policy carries the opening day. Code & Country puts regulators, members of Congress and industry executives on the same stage to discuss legislation, stablecoin rules, energy infrastructure and civil liberties.

Corporate treasury strategy is the second thread. The Bitcoin for Corporations Symposium runs on April 27 at The Venetian for Pro and Whale Pass holders, aimed at public-company executives and capital allocators.

The third is the overlap between mining and AI compute. The Energy Stage and the new Compute Village give miners, data center operators and energy companies their own corner of the floor.

## How to attend Bitcoin 2026

Three pass types are on sale through the [official ticketing page](https://tickets.b.tc/event/bitcoin-2026/tickets). General Admission covers April 28 and 29 only, with entry to the main stage, the Genesis Stage and the expo hall. The Pro Pass adds Pro Day on April 27, the Enterprise Hall and Enterprise Stage, the symposium and a Pro Pass reception. The Whale Pass adds The Deep lounge, Whale Night and all official after parties. Students can apply for a free General Admission pass.

Anyone who wants the regulators' sessions on Monday needs a Pro or Whale Pass.

Bitcoin Week runs April 26 to 29 around the conference, with the Women of Bitcoin Bash, a poker tournament, the symposium and nightly official after parties on the organizer's calendar. Powerclub Global covers the Bitcoin Conference as a media partner of BTC Inc, and our [Bitcoin 2026 side events guide](/press/bitcoin-2026-las-vegas-side-events) will list the events worth adding.

## Frequently asked questions

### When is Bitcoin 2026?

Bitcoin 2026 takes place Monday, April 27 through Wednesday, April 29, 2026. April 27 is Pro Day, open to Pro and Whale Pass holders. General Admission passes are valid on April 28 and 29.

### Where is Bitcoin 2026 held?

The conference is at The Venetian Convention and Expo Center, 3355 S Las Vegas Blvd, Las Vegas, Nevada. The Venetian is also the official hotel partner for the event, with a booking link on the conference site.

### Who is speaking at Bitcoin 2026?

Confirmed speakers include SEC Chairman Paul Atkins, CFTC Chairman Mike Selig, Senator Cynthia Lummis, Michael Saylor of Strategy, Jack Mallers of Strike and Twenty One, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino and Blockstream CEO Adam Back.

### How much are Bitcoin 2026 tickets?

Pass prices as listed on the official site on April 16, 2026: General Admission $549, Pro Pass $1,499 and Whale Pass $10,999. Check the official ticketing page for the current figure.

Selig was sworn in as the 16th chairman of the CFTC on December 22, 2025, after serving as chief counsel of the SEC's Crypto Task Force. His fireside conversation is on the Nakamoto Stage on Monday at 11:00 am, moderated by Gregory Xethalis of Multicoin Capital.

Mallers runs the payments company Strike and has led Twenty One Capital as chief executive since December 2025. His keynote is on the Nakamoto Stage on Wednesday, April 29 at 3:50 pm, one of the last major slots of the conference. BTC Inc runs one official party each night: the Kickoff Party at LIV Nightclub on Monday (10:30 pm to 3:00 am), Omnia on Tuesday (10:30 pm to 3:00 am, with Steve Aoki billed after midnight) and Tao on Wednesday (10:30 pm to 1:00 am). Bitcoin Week runs April 26 to 29. The first events are on Sunday evening, April 26, before Pro Day, and the last official after party is at Tao on Wednesday, April 29.

Not always. The Run for Hal is open to all, and the Circa takeover needs no conference pass. The official poker tournament and the BitGo summit require a Bitcoin 2026 pass, and the pass-holder receptions require a Pro or Whale Pass.

Miami Beach — Consensus 2026, CoinDesk's flagship crypto conference, runs May 5 to 7 at the Miami Beach Convention Center, its first edition in Miami after Toronto in 2025 and a Hong Kong event in February. CoinDesk expects more than 20,000 attendees from over 100 countries, and it has built the program around institutional finance, stablecoins and AI agents that pay for things. For founders, investors and marketers, it puts regulators, banks and builders in one building for three days.

The published agenda puts a regulator, a bank and several founders on the main stage on day one. Michael Selig, chairman of the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission, has a fireside on Tuesday afternoon. Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse is interviewed by Bullish CEO Tom Farley that morning, and Amy Oldenburg, head of digital asset strategy at Morgan Stanley, follows after lunch. Solana co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko and Cloudflare chief strategy officer Stephanie Cohen both have Tuesday firesides.

The city is the first change. CoinDesk's press page describes this edition as the conference's Miami debut, and its March 10 announcement framed the move as a return to the United States. Solana Accelerate USA also takes place on May 5 as part of the Consensus program.

body:
Miami — Mining Disrupt 2026 opens at the Miami Airport Convention Center on July 21 and runs through July 23, with an opening evening of networking followed by two days of keynotes, panels and a Bitcoin mining expo. It matters this year because the program treats mining and AI compute as one infrastructure business: the same power, land and cooling now serve both, and the people who buy, host and finance that capacity will be on one floor.

## At a glance

- Dates: July 21 to 23, 2026 (pre-party and pass-holder events on July 21; keynotes and expo on July 22 and 23)
- Venue: Miami Airport Convention Center at the DoubleTree by Hilton Miami Airport and Convention Center, 711 NW 72nd Avenue, Miami, Florida
- Organizer: Mining Disrupt, which has run Bitcoin mining events since 2019
- Expected scale: thousands of attendees (organizer-reported)
- Format: two days of keynotes, fireside chats and panels beside an expo floor, plus official evening events
- Official site: [miningdisrupt.com](https://miningdisrupt.com/)

## What Mining Disrupt 2026 covers

The organizer bills Mining Disrupt as the world's largest Bitcoin mining expo, and the Miami show is its eighth year. The December [announcement of the 2026 dates](https://btcwire.io/newsroom/mining-disrupt-2026-returns-to-miami-as-the-worlds-premier-bitcoin-mining-ai-conference/) framed it as a Bitcoin mining and AI conference, and the published topic list follows through. The [Mining Disrupt 2026 conference page](/conferences/mining-disrupt-2026) has the background.

Eight themes are listed: AI and high-performance computing, quantum computing and security, energy innovation, heat reuse, the open-source movement, the home mining revival, the repair economy, and sovereignty and nodes. Panel titles are already public. They include:

- Decrypt or Die: quantum computing versus Bitcoin security
- GPUs Ate My ASIC: why Bitcoin miners are pivoting to AI infrastructure
- Trash to Hash: turning waste energy into Bitcoin
- Fork Around and Find Out: open-source mining versus closed hardware makers
- The ASIC Underground: repair, refurbishment and extending miner lifespans

## How the three days are scheduled

The official schedule splits the show in two. Tuesday, July 21 is the social opening: the Official Pre-Party is open to all passes, and Genesis pass holders have a cigar and cocktail lounge from 5:00 pm and the Genesis Dinner from 7:00 pm, both by RSVP.

Wednesday, July 22 is Day 1 of the conference, with breakfast, keynotes and the expo, and the Official After-Party in the evening. Thursday, July 23 is Day 2, with breakfast, keynotes, the expo and a movie screening open to all passes. Speakers had not been assigned to published time slots when this was written, so check the organizer's agenda before fixing meetings around a session.

## Who is on the Mining Disrupt 2026 program

The newest additions to the speaker list lean toward operators and the companies that keep sites running. HIVE Digital Technologies is sending chief operating officer Luke Rossy and Gabriel Lamas, its country president for Paraguay. Steven Eliscu, chief operating officer of DMG Blockchain Solutions, adds a second listed miner.

On energy, Rapha Zagury, founder and CEO of Elektron Energy, and David Chernis, who directs flexible compute platforms at CPower, cover power sourcing and grid programs. Braiins, VNISH, OBM and FARMGOD represent firmware, pools and fleet software. Our [guide to the Mining Disrupt 2026 speakers](/press/mining-disrupt-2026-miami-featured-speakers) profiles twelve of them.

On the expo floor, more than 100 sponsor brands were listed on the official site in mid-June, from ASIC makers and resellers to hosting providers, cooling and filtration suppliers, pools and firmware teams.

## How to attend

Tickets are sold through the organizer's [Eventbrite page for Mining Disrupt 2026](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/mining-disrupt-conference-2026-miami-florida-tickets-1969885866655). There are three access levels:

- Satoshi Access (general): keynotes and expo, the official opening and after-party, the container showcase, the movie screening and the breakfast buffet
- Miner Access (VIP): everything in Satoshi, plus the Miner VIP lounge, an open bar and a cigar lounge
- Genesis Access (elite): everything in Miner, plus a private Genesis lounge, backstage and speaker access, and the Genesis private dinner

The organizer says Miner and Genesis levels are limited and usually sell out first. It offers group rates for parties of ten or more and visa invitation letters on request, and its policy is no refunds.

## Mining Disrupt 2026 speakers from listed miners

### Luke Rossy, Chief Operating Officer, HIVE Digital Technologies

Rossy has run operations at HIVE since January 2024, after serving as its vice president of operations. HIVE is a Nasdaq-listed miner with sites in Canada, Sweden and Paraguay. He is the person to hear on how a listed operator brings new capacity online and keeps it running.

### Gabriel Lamas, Country President of Paraguay, HIVE Digital Technologies

Lamas, an electrical engineer with more than 20 years in infrastructure and energy projects, joined HIVE in March 2025 to [lead its operations and expansion in Paraguay](https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/244817/HIVE-Digital-Technologies-Welcomes-Gabriel-Lamas-as-Country-President-of-Paraguay). He previously led Latin American infrastructure and operations at Bitfarms. Anyone weighing sites in South America should hear him.

### Steven Eliscu, Chief Operating Officer, DMG Blockchain Solutions

Eliscu [became DMG's chief operating officer in 2022](https://www.dmgblockchain.com/p/steven-eliscu-joins-as-coo) after sitting on its board, and earlier worked in finance and investor relations at Bitfury USA. DMG is a publicly traded miner based in Vancouver. He is well placed to speak on how a mid-sized miner funds new infrastructure.

## Hardware, firmware and fleet software

### Irene Gao, President of Mining, Bitmain

Gao leads the global mining business at Bitmain, the world's largest maker of crypto mining hardware, and speaks for the company at industry events. Hardware supply shapes every other decision on the floor, so buyers should treat her remarks as a guide to pricing and efficiency.

### Ryan Miller, Director of Business Development, Braiins

Miller works on the commercial side of Braiins, the company behind Braiins OS firmware and Braiins Pool. One of the organizer's published panels sets open-source mining against closed hardware makers, and Braiins has a stake in that debate. His team is who operators call when they want to tune a fleet.

### Bradley Peak, Global Head of Sales, VNISH

Peak sells VNISH's aftermarket ASIC firmware, which operators use to tune power draw and hash rate. VNISH is co-hosting the opening-night party with the EMCD mining pool, covered in our [side events guide](/press/mining-disrupt-2026-miami-side-events). He is a good contact for operators trying to get more from machines they already own.

### Dan Lawrence, Chief Executive Officer, OBM

Lawrence co-founded [OBM](https://obm.io/about/), the company behind Foreman, a platform for managing mining fleets remotely, after 15 years as a technical director at the U.S. Department of Defense. OBM now builds tools for flexible load management across mining and AI sites, which ties his work to the energy sessions.

## Energy and the grid

### Rapha Zagury, Founder and CEO, Elektron Energy

Zagury founded Elektron Energy, a Bitcoin mining and infrastructure company, after a Wall Street career that included roles at Goldman Sachs, Merrill Lynch and Deutsche Bank. He brings a capital-markets view of power: what a megawatt is worth to a miner, and who should own it.

### David Chernis, Director of Flexible Compute Platforms, CPower

Chernis leads CPower's work with mining and high-performance computing sites that take part in demand response, cutting load when the grid is tight. He was previously an energy projects manager at Amazon Web Services, working on power procurement for data centers. For operators, flexibility is a second income line.

## Operations, facilities and the floor

### Dan Koehler, Chief Executive Officer, ASIC Plug and FARMGOD

Koehler runs ASIC Plug, a mining hardware supplier, and FARMGOD, a monitoring and management platform for mining farms. He also spoke at the organizer's Texas summit in November 2025. Operators comparing fleet-management tools can hear from a founder who sells the machines as well as the software that watches them.

### Adam Wiggins, Director of Data Center Solutions, Camfil

Wiggins has spent more than a decade on air filtration systems at Camfil, a clean-air manufacturer, and now focuses on data centers. Dust and contamination wear down air-cooled miners and servers alike, which makes filtration a cost question tied to the organizer's repair and lifespan theme.

### Max Matrenitski, Founder, Everminer and Cyberian Mine

Matrenitski founded Cyberian Mine, a Bitcoin mining company in Germany, and launched Everminer in 2024 with prepaid lifetime mining contracts. The organizer also lists him as founder of OpenMine. He speaks for the retail end of the market, the audience behind the home mining panels.

Hardware buyers should start with Gao, Miller and Peak. Anyone choosing a power strategy or a hosting partner should follow Zagury, Chernis and Lawrence.

Hong Kong — Bitcoin Asia 2026 opens at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre in Wan Chai on August 27 and 28, with the full agenda published and Changpeng Zhao added to the lineup on August 3. Organizer BTC Inc expects more than 10,000 attendees, and this year it has built a dedicated business program around the main stages, which makes the two days as useful for companies raising capital as for people who come for the keynotes.

## Who is speaking at Bitcoin Asia 2026

The organizer's headliners are Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, Network School founder Balaji Srinivasan and Metaplanet CEO Simon Gerovich. BTC Inc announced Zhao on August 3, the day it released the [full two-day agenda](https://asia.b.tc/agenda). He speaks Thursday afternoon on the Nakamoto Stage, the main stage, in The Bitcoin Century.

The first wave of names, announced in June, set the range of the program: Dr. Johnny Ng of Hong Kong's Legislative Council, who gives the opening-morning keynote; Bilal Bin Saqib, Chairman of the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority; Bitget CEO Gracy Chen; TRON founder Justin Sun; and David Bailey, CEO and Chairman of Nakamoto Inc. The biggest addition is on the business side. In a [July 27 release](https://btcmedia.prowly.com/466346-bitcoin-asia-2026-brings-full-enterprise-and-business-development-track-to-hong-kong), BTC Inc laid out an institutional program that shares one floor of the HKCEC on August 27:

- The Bitcoin for Corporations Symposium, a day of sessions on treasury strategy, governance, capital formation and custody.

There is also something for collectors. BMAG, the arts division of BTC Inc, will debut a [Trading Card Expo](https://asia.b.tc/card-expo) on the conference floor, with a vendor marketplace, tournaments with Bitcoin prizes, live pack openings and on-site grading.

## Treasury companies and regulators set the themes

BTC Inc says the programming centers on the meeting of Eastern and Western Bitcoin markets, with sessions on monetary policy, corporate treasury strategy, infrastructure and regulation across Asia.

Policy runs from Thursday's Hong Kong keynote to a Friday session on special economic zones with Bin Saqib and Invest Hong Kong's King Leung. The Genesis Stage opens Thursday with a block of Chinese-language panels, and the Open Source Hub runs hands-on workshops both days.

Passes come in three levels: General Admission, GA+ and the Whale Pass. BTC Inc's July 27 release listed GA+ at $187; it adds the Deal Flow Zone, in-app meeting scheduling and priority main stage seating. The Symposium requires a GA+ or Whale Pass, and Deal Day is by application.

Expect vinyl, cocktails and food, payable in sats. One house rule: do not ask how much anyone holds. Free, with host approval on Luma. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/4wvwlqbf)

## Bitcoin Asia 2026 side events on day one: August 27

### Deal Day

BTC Inc's Deal Day runs 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM at the HKCEC: pre-scheduled 30-minute meetings between Bitcoin companies and banks, funds and analysts, with a lunch panel and a closing reception. The Las Vegas edition matched 23 presenting companies with 23 investing partners (organizer-reported). Invitation only, by application. [Register or see details](https://asia.b.tc/deal-day)

### Bitcoin for Corporations Symposium

The Symposium opens at 10:00 AM in Meeting Room N101 with sessions on treasury mechanics, governance, custody and financing for corporate decision-makers and allocators. Organizer pages give two end times, 3:00 PM and 4:00 PM; the agenda lists BFC Stage sessions until just after 4:00 PM. A GA+ or Whale Pass is required. [Register or see details](https://bitcoinforcorporations.com/events/hong-kong-symposium-2026/)

### Whale Night, hosted by Antalpha

The official evening for Whale Pass holders runs 8:00 to 11:00 PM at Cloud 39. The organizer bills it as an evening of fire and fortune and asks guests to wear red. Whale Pass holders also get a reception hosted by Bitmain on Wednesday, August 26, 7:00 to 9:00 PM in the Pool Room at Soho House Hong Kong.

## Bitcoin Asia 2026 side events on day two: August 28

### AI x BTC

OnePiece Labs and OP_CAT Layer, with co-hosts including ClawChat, OffChain Global and Web3Labs, run an afternoon of demos and debate on AI agents, Bitcoin infrastructure and BIP-110. The hosts' page gives 12:30 to 6:00 PM at the CAI Building, 54 to 58 Electric Road, Tin Hau. Free on Luma, and the most builder-focused event here. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/btchk26oc)

### Power Salon: A Dialogue on Mining and AI Data Centers

Mining pool EMCD and DMA host this salon from 2:00 to 6:00 PM on power, site selection, hardware and the economics shared by Bitcoin mining and AI data centers. It is aimed at miners, data center operators, energy providers and investors. Registration is screened, and the address is released on approval. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/usps10z2)

### To the Moon: The Elite BTC Networking

Web3Labs, with Forthright Securities and Moon Inc, hosts a private networking evening from 6:00 to 10:00 PM at 60 Wyndham Street, Central, aimed at funds, large holders and founders. Free places are limited and reviewed by the host; a $199 ticket skips the review. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/sf7kmcwx)

### OnlyBulls After Dark

Rare Network and OnlyBulls host a rooftop happy hour from 7:00 to 10:00 PM at FAYY, on the 26th floor of California Tower, 30 to 32 D'Aguilar Street, Central, with light food, an open bar and a DJ. Entry is free with registration and capped at 230 people. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/dl889os6)

### Official After Party

The conference's own closing party runs from 7:30 PM to 1:00 AM at Dragon-i. The official listing prices entry at $50, sold through BTC Inc's ticket page, and the Whale Pass includes after-party access. [Register or see details](https://tickets.b.tc/event/bitcoin-asia-2026)

## How to plan the week

For capital, Deal Day and the Symposium are the organizer's own business program. For builders, AI x BTC and the Power Salon overlap on Friday afternoon, so choose one. Session times are in our [Bitcoin Asia 2026 speakers guide](/press/bitcoin-asia-2026-featured-speakers), and dates and passes are in the [Bitcoin Asia 2026 preview](/press/bitcoin-asia-2026-hong-kong-pre-event). Powerclub Global covers Bitcoin Asia as a media partner of BTC Inc and will publish session coverage and short-form video from the event.

### How do I get into Bitcoin Asia 2026 side events?

It depends on the event. The 5K run, AI x BTC and OnlyBulls After Dark take free registration on Luma. The pre-conference meetup and the Power Salon need host approval. Deal Day is invitation only, the Symposium needs a GA+ or Whale Pass, and Whale Night needs a Whale Pass.

Many are. The 5K run, the pre-conference meetup, AI x BTC, the Power Salon and OnlyBulls After Dark list no charge. The Official After Party is listed at $50, and To the Moon offers a $199 ticket alongside free places that the host reviews.

### Is there an official Bitcoin Asia 2026 after party?

Yes. The Official After Party is on Friday, August 28, 2026, from 7:30 PM to 1:00 AM at Dragon-i. Entry is ticketed at $50 on the official listing, and the Whale Pass includes after-party access.

title: TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026: Dates, Speakers, What to Expect
description: TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026 runs October 7-8 at Marina Bay Sands. Dates, confirmed speakers, ticket prices, the main themes and how to plan the week.
body:
Singapore — TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026 opens at Marina Bay Sands on Wednesday, October 7, and runs through Thursday, October 8, with TOKEN2049 Week filling the city from October 5 to 11. The organizer reports more than 25,000 attendees from over 160 countries, which makes this the one week of the year when exchanges, asset managers, founders and investors from most of the crypto industry are in the same building. Details below are as of October 1.

## At a glance

- Dates: October 7-8, 2026, 7:30 am to 6:00 pm daily
- TOKEN2049 Week: October 5-11, 2026
- Venue: Marina Bay Sands, 10 Bayfront Avenue, Singapore
- Expected scale (organizer-reported): 25,000+ attendees, 7,000+ companies, 300+ speakers, 500+ exhibitors, 1,000+ side events
- Stages: OKX Main Stage, BingX Labs Stage, MEXC Stage and Bit Digital Stage, plus an approval-only Institutional Stage on October 8
- Official site: [token2049.com/singapore](https://www.token2049.com/singapore)

## Who is speaking at TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026

The [official agenda](https://www.token2049.com/singapore/agenda) puts the best-known names on the OKX Main Stage. On Wednesday, Balaji Srinivasan opens with a keynote at 9:10 am and moderates a fireside chat with Polymarket founder and CEO Shayne Coplan at 9:30. Hyperliquid Labs CEO Jeff Yan follows at 11:00 and Maelstrom CIO Arthur Hayes at 11:35. The afternoon includes Eric Trump of World Liberty Financial on a 2:00 pm panel, Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss of Gemini at 3:00 pm, and firesides with Formula 1 drivers Lando Norris and Max Verstappen.

Thursday leans institutional. Franklin Templeton CEO Jenny Johnson and Binance co-CEO Richard Teng open the day at 9:10 am, Nasdaq chair and CEO Adena Friedman sits for a fireside chat at 2:00 pm, and executives from BlackRock, Fidelity, Morgan Stanley, Bitwise and ICE close the main stage with a tokenization panel at 4:20 pm.

The organizer's site also lists Vitalik Buterin and Robinhood's Vlad Tenev among its headline speakers. Neither had a session on the published agenda as of October 1. The [TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026 speakers guide](/press/token2049-singapore-2026-featured-speakers) picks 14 sessions to plan around, and the [conference page](/conferences/token2049-singapore-2026) has the event summary.

## What is on the program beyond the main stage

- TOKEN2049 Institutional: a private gathering on October 8 for 200 individually approved participants from global finance and digital assets, primarily managing-director level and above. It has its own Institutional Stage, and attendance is by approval.
- NEXUS Startup Competition: ten finalists, chosen from more than 1,000 applicants, pitch for a US$250,000 prize pool. The first round is Wednesday at 5:00 pm on the MEXC Stage and the final is Thursday at 3:00 pm, with judges from Dragonfly, Maelstrom and Multicoin Capital.
- Origins Hackathon: a 36-hour build sprint, with demos on the MEXC Stage on Thursday at 4:00 pm.

## The themes: institutional money and AI agents

Two subjects run through both days. The first is traditional finance moving onchain: Thursday's main stage covers tokenized assets, cross-border regulation and stablecoin payments, and the Institutional Stage adds sessions with Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, CME Group and BlackRock. The second is AI. Wednesday's main stage carries a 4:35 pm panel titled "The Agent Economy: Why AI Needs Crypto," and the smaller stages add keynotes on agentic trading.

## Privacy gets main-stage time

Privacy is the third thread. Zcash has a keynote from Zooko of Shielded Labs on Wednesday morning and a main-stage panel, "The Zcash Moment," at 3:00 pm. Midnight, the privacy blockchain from the Cardano ecosystem and a Gold sponsor on the official [partners page](https://www.token2049.com/singapore/partners), has two keynotes: its president, Fahmi Syed, speaks on the Bit Digital Stage on Wednesday at 11:45 am, and Charles Hoskinson, founder and CEO of Input Output, delivers "Midnight City" on the OKX Main Stage on Thursday at 9:40 am.

## How to attend TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026

Tickets were in their final release when checked on October 1. The Last Bird pass costs US$699 and covers the stages, the exhibition and complimentary access to Sui Basecamp. The Special Access Pass costs US$4,999 and adds TOKEN2049 Institutional, the Speakers Reception and guaranteed entry to the closing party. Tickets are non-refundable, according to the [official FAQ](https://www.token2049.com/singapore/faqs).

Side events are separate. Each host runs its own registration, and the organizer's listing at [week.token2049.com](https://week.token2049.com) is the place to browse them. The companion [guide to TOKEN2049 Singapore side events](/press/token2049-singapore-2026-side-events) gives a shortlist with access status for each.

## Frequently asked questions

### When is TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026?

TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026 takes place on Wednesday, October 7 and Thursday, October 8, 2026. Each day runs from 7:30 am to 6:00 pm. TOKEN2049 Week runs from October 5 to 11.

### Where is TOKEN2049 Singapore held?

The conference is held at Marina Bay Sands, 10 Bayfront Avenue, Singapore 018956. The venue sits on the Marina Bay waterfront, and the organizer says the 2026 edition takes over all five floors.

### Who is speaking at TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026?

The agenda includes Adena Friedman of Nasdaq, Jenny Johnson of Franklin Templeton, Shayne Coplan of Polymarket, Jeff Yan of Hyperliquid Labs, Arthur Hayes and Balaji Srinivasan. The organizer reports more than 300 speakers.

### How much are TOKEN2049 Singapore tickets?

As of October 1, 2026, the Last Bird pass was US$699 and the Special Access Pass was US$4,999. Both were described as the final release, and tickets are non-refundable.

The next edition is [TOKEN2049 Dubai on April 21-22, 2027](/conferences/token2049-dubai-2027). body:
Singapore — TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026 runs October 7-8 at Marina Bay Sands, and the organizer reports more than 300 speakers across its stages. The useful question is which sessions justify leaving a meeting. These 14 speakers cover the subjects most attendees came for: institutional money, stablecoins, AI, Ethereum and privacy. Stages and times are as printed on the official agenda on October 1 and can still move.

## At a glance

- Dates: October 7-8, 2026 (Wednesday and Thursday)
- Venue: Marina Bay Sands, Singapore
- Expected scale (organizer-reported): 300+ speakers, 25,000+ attendees
- Access note: Institutional Stage sessions are for approved TOKEN2049 Institutional participants only
- Official agenda: [TOKEN2049 Singapore agenda](https://www.token2049.com/singapore/agenda)
- Official site: [token2049.com/singapore](https://www.token2049.com/singapore)

## Wall Street arrives at TOKEN2049 Singapore

### Adena Friedman, Chair and CEO, Nasdaq

Friedman runs one of the world's largest exchange operators. Her fireside chat is on the OKX Main Stage on Thursday at 2:00 pm, moderated by CNBC managing editor Joanna Ossinger. At 2:40 pm she joins Kraken co-CEO Arjun Sethi on the approval-only Institutional Stage for "24/7 Markets: The Future of Global Trading."

### Jenny Johnson, CEO, Franklin Templeton

Johnson leads a global asset manager and opens Thursday on the OKX Main Stage at 9:10 am in "The New Institutional Market: Tokenized Assets. Global Liquidity. Onchain Settlement," with Binance co-CEO Richard Teng. At 10:20 am she joins Tom Lee on the Institutional Stage for "The Next Wave of Institutional Capital."

### Nikhil Sharma, Director, Digital Assets, BlackRock

Sharma appears twice on Thursday afternoon. At 3:20 pm he joins a tokenization panel on the Institutional Stage, and at 4:20 pm he is on the closing OKX Main Stage panel, "Tokenization: The Next Investment Revolution," with executives from Fidelity Investments, Bitwise, Morgan Stanley and ICE.

### Timothy Moe, Chief Asia Pacific Equity Strategist, Goldman Sachs

Moe moderates "The New Macro Order: Liquidity, Capital and Digital Assets," a 20-minute fireside with Zoltan Pozsar of Ex Uno Plures, on Thursday at 10:00 am. It opens the Institutional Stage, so it is limited to approved participants. Pozsar also appears on the OKX Main Stage on Wednesday at 4:00 pm.

## Stablecoins, payments and policy

### May Zabaneh, SVP, PayPal

Zabaneh speaks on "Stablecoins: The Payments Industry, Rebuilt" on the OKX Main Stage on Thursday at 11:10 am, with MoonPay founder and CEO Ivan Soto-Wright and Rain co-founder and CEO Farooq Malik. It is the main-stage session on how payments companies are putting stablecoins to work.

### Charles Cascarilla, Co-Founder and CEO, Paxos

Cascarilla leads Paxos, a stablecoin and tokenization infrastructure company. He joins "From the White House to Wall Street: What's Next for Crypto?" on the BingX Labs Stage on Wednesday at 2:50 pm, with Kraken's Arjun Sethi, Pantera Capital president Scott Lawin and Jake Chervinsky of the Hyperliquid Policy Center.

### Deepa Raja Carbon, Vice Chair and Managing Director, VARA

Carbon helps lead VARA, Dubai's virtual assets regulator. She sits on "Regulation: Finding Clarity Across Borders" on the OKX Main Stage on Thursday at 10:00 am with Arjun Sethi, Jake Chervinsky and Brian Quintenz, then leads "Why Dubai Wins" on the BingX Labs Stage at noon.

## AI and crypto speakers to watch

### Emad Mostaque, Founder and CEO, Intelligent Internet

Mostaque gives a keynote titled "Intelligence You Own, Not Rent" on the BingX Labs Stage on Wednesday at 10:40 am. He returns at 4:35 pm on the OKX Main Stage for "The Agent Economy: Why AI Needs Crypto," a panel with Illia Polosukhin and Jesse Pollak of Base.

### Illia Polosukhin, Co-Founder, NEAR Protocol

Polosukhin speaks on "Making AI and Finance Private by Default" on the BingX Labs Stage on Wednesday at 11:20 am. He then joins the 4:35 pm agent-economy panel on the OKX Main Stage. The two slots cover where AI agents meet onchain payments and privacy.

### Magnus Grimeland, Founder and CEO, Antler

Grimeland runs Antler, the early-stage venture firm founded in Singapore. His 15-minute keynote, "The Center of Gravity Has Moved: Asia's AI & Crypto Decade," is on the Bit Digital Stage on Wednesday at 4:15 pm. Founders raising in the region get an investor's view of where early-stage capital is heading.

## Ethereum and infrastructure

### Steven Goldfeder, Co-Founder and CEO, Offchain Labs

Goldfeder leads Offchain Labs, the company behind the Arbitrum network. He has a 15-minute keynote on the Bit Digital Stage on Wednesday at 10:30 am. The agenda lists it only as "Keynote," so the topic is unannounced. Developers building on Ethereum layer-2 networks should hold the slot.

### Joseph Lubin, Co-Founder, Ethereum

Lubin, listed on the agenda as Ethereum co-founder and MetaMask chairman and CEO, joins "Ethereum's Next Act: From Asset to Economy" on the OKX Main Stage on Thursday at noon with Morpho's Paul Frambot and Bit Digital CEO Sam Tabar. At 2:40 pm he returns for a panel on real-world assets with Robinhood's Johann Kerbrat.

## Privacy keynotes at TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026

### Fahmi Syed, President, Midnight

Syed is president of Midnight, a privacy blockchain from the Cardano ecosystem and a Gold sponsor on the official partners page. His 15-minute keynote is on the Bit Digital Stage on Wednesday at 11:45 am, with no title published yet. It is one of several privacy sessions that day, alongside talks from Zcash and NEAR.

### Charles Hoskinson, Founder and CEO, Input Output

Hoskinson founded Input Output, the engineering company behind Cardano and Midnight. His keynote, "Midnight City," is on the OKX Main Stage on Thursday from 9:40 to 10:00 am, directly after the opening panel with Jenny Johnson. That gives a privacy network a main-stage slot on the most institution-heavy morning.

## Frequently asked questions

### Who is speaking at TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026?

The agenda includes Adena Friedman of Nasdaq, Jenny Johnson of Franklin Templeton, Shayne Coplan of Polymarket, Jeff Yan of Hyperliquid Labs, Arthur Hayes, Balaji Srinivasan and Joseph Lubin. The organizer reports more than 300 speakers, and the full list is on the [official speakers page](https://www.token2049.com/singapore/speakers).

### When is TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026?

The conference takes place on Wednesday, October 7 and Thursday, October 8, 2026, at Marina Bay Sands. Doors open at 7:30 am and the first sessions start at 9:00 am. TOKEN2049 Week runs from October 5 to 11.

### Which day is best for institutional sessions?

Thursday, October 8, at Marina Bay Sands. The OKX Main Stage carries Franklin Templeton at 9:10 am, PayPal at 11:10 am, Nasdaq at 2:00 pm and the tokenization panel at 4:20 pm.

## TOKEN2049 Singapore side events before the conference opens

### 0G Dev Day: ZERO TO INFINITY

Hosted by the 0G Foundation on Monday, October 5, from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm at National Gallery Singapore. It is a full day of keynotes, panels and demos on AI agents, with Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How as guest of honor. It suits AI and crypto builders arriving early. Free; standard registration was open as of October 1, the VIP breakfast tier was full, and the speakers reception needs approval. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/0g-devday-2026)

## Side events on the TOKEN2049 conference days, October 7 and 8

### Digital Asset Summit Asia 2026

Blockworks runs its one-day institutional conference on Wednesday, October 7, at Marina Bay Sands. Listed speakers include Justin Sun, Richard Teng of Binance, Liz Martin of Coinbase Institutional, Mike Belshe of BitGo and executives from Fidelity Investments, Morgan Stanley and DBS Digital Exchange. Blockworks reports 750+ attendees and 500+ institutions. Ticketed: as of October 1 only the last-chance tiers remained, at US$899 for general admission and US$1,699 for VIP, and allocator passes were sold out. [Register or see details](https://blockworks.com/event/digital-asset-summit-asia)

### Circle House

Circle hosts a two-day open house on October 7 and 8, 9:30 am to 5:00 pm, on Level 3 of the Marina Bay Sands Expo and Convention Centre. Live demos and partner sessions cover USDC, Arc and onchain finance, so it suits payments and stablecoin teams. Free; the event page says no TOKEN2049 pass is required, but every guest must register in advance for a QR code. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/circlehouse2026)

### Sui Basecamp 2026

Sui's own conference runs October 7 and 8 at Marina Bay Sands, built around agentic finance, with four stages and speakers including Evan Cheng of Mysten Labs, Raoul Pal, Richard Socher and Brian Quintenz. It suits developers and investors following the Sui ecosystem. Ticketed: the last-call tier was US$299 as of October 1, and the TOKEN2049 FAQ says the standard conference pass includes complimentary Basecamp access. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/SuiBasecamp2026)

## Privacy and founder events during TOKEN2049 week

### Privacy Summit

An afternoon on crypto privacy and compliance on Wednesday, October 7, from 1:00 to 7:00 pm at Paya Lebar Quarter (PLQ 3), away from the Marina Bay venue. The event page says it is organized by StarkWare. Topics include private payments and what regulated institutions need before using public blockchains, with live product demos. It suits privacy engineers, wallet teams and compliance leads. Free; registration is subject to host approval. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/gbb4thfy)

### Rooftop UTXO Pitch Night

A live pitch competition for founders building on Cardano, Bitcoin and other UTXO networks, presented by Draper and Cardano on Wednesday, October 7, from 6:30 to 11:00 pm at LAVO, on Level 57 of Marina Bay Sands. The page states up to US$500,000 in total funding, awarded at the investors' discretion, followed by rooftop networking. It suits early-stage founders and the investors who back them. Free; approval required, with places still open as of October 1. [Register or see details](https://luma.com/utxopitchnight)

### Midnight at TOKEN2049 Singapore

Midnight, the privacy blockchain from the Cardano ecosystem and a Gold sponsor of the conference, hosts three public events. On Thursday, October 8, [Midnight Cafe](https://luma.com/rvb1kraj) runs from 10:30 am to 5:30 pm at Maison Boulud in The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands, with demos and open registration. [Privacy Pitched](https://luma.com/vxg0nlpp) takes over the cafe from 1:00 to 4:00 pm: a keynote, demos from teams building on Midnight and questions from investors, also open registration. ENTER THE NIGHT, an approval-only networking evening on Wednesday at 6:00 pm, was nearly at capacity as of October 1. A Thursday investor brunch is invite-only.

## The official TOKEN2049 closing party

### AFTER 2049

The organizer's closing party is on Friday, October 9, from 7:00 pm at the Marina Bay Sands SkyPark Observation Deck on the 57th floor. Claptone headlines, with Crusy, ANONM, Leon, Milam and Mo-Shi. It suits teams that want one last evening with contacts as the Singapore Grand Prix weekend begins. Ticketed, 18 and over, smart casual: the first release sold out and the ticket page listed a final release for October 2. [Register or see details](https://megatix.com.sg/events/after2049)

Apply now for anything that needs approval, because approval-only events fill before the week starts. On the conference days, the [TOKEN2049 Singapore speakers guide](/press/token2049-singapore-2026-featured-speakers) shows which sessions are worth protecting, and the [pre-event overview](/press/token2049-singapore-2026-pre-event) covers dates, tickets and the program.

### How do I get into TOKEN2049 Singapore side events?

Register on each event's own page. Many are free but require host approval, so apply early, and a few sell tickets. The organizer lists side events at week.token2049.com. Registration is separate from the conference pass.

TOKEN2049 Week runs from Monday, October 5 to Sunday, October 11, 2026. The conference itself is October 7-8, and the official closing party, AFTER 2049, is on Friday, October 9. The Singapore Grand Prix weekend follows from October 9 to 11.
